Almost all of the stuff here is true even if this video felt a bit "brain-washy". Alternate nuclear fuels have been a talking point since the first power plant but back in the day and even today to a lesser extent the fact you could get bombs from spend energy trumped discussions of efficiency and sustainability.

These days when nobody want to use nuclear weapons really these kind of alternate ideas are taking shape with thorium being pretty high up there. It would mean very different power plants which means big up front investment for refits or new builds but it would make energy so much cheaper with less danger to the surrounding area than a coal plant.

A few of the other ideas mentioned in this video are less sturdy, a lot of blue sky thinking that I doubt the numbers would match up with. But after a loss of money energy networks would see cheaper running that would only get cheaper as time went on, spurring bigger and bigger power stations as the supply could be met very easily and the danger would minimal. With that much power being produces the prices would drop dramatically across the world as it was traded internationally, having electrical power could very easily be a human right at that stage and I wouldn't be surprised if a decade after this technology was first used on an international level if residential consumption was considered free or at least covered by taxes as the price would be so low.
I heard China has been working on developing Thorium Nuclear Energy, but I think there's a few problems that there trying to solve before it becomes mainstream.
